pos.personaBrief: Sebes's side used the ball as its main weapon: Hidegkuti's deep movement and quick passing kept Hungary in control of games (Wikipedia, guidetofootball), and the team wanted the ball rather than ceding it on purpose.

pro.personaBrief: The team built through short, rotating combinations and Bozsik pushing into space (guidetofootball), not long balls to a free striker, but its attacks were fast once possession was won, as Puskás's remark about attacking together suggests.

est.personaBrief: The defining fact is fluidity: Hidegkuti withdrew from centre forward, wingers dropped back, Hidegkuti moved to outside left in the 1954 semi-final, and Sebes wanted players able to play any position (Wikipedia, TFT). Fixed zones are rejected.

lar.personaBrief: Hungary's attacks ran through the middle: the centre forward dropped deep and inside forwards attacked the space he opened, while the wingers tucked in (guidetofootball). Wide play came from rotation, not from traditional touchline wingers.

blo.personaBrief: The verified evidence speaks of attacking with the whole team and of drawing defenders out, but pressing is not verified; the gap is noted. The profile prefers to win the ball and attack, and to press its own mistakes back quickly, rather than to sit deep (general knowledge for the pressing part).

mar.personaBrief: Hungary's own marking is not verified; the only evidence is that opposing centre-halves followed Hidegkuti into midfield (Wikipedia, guidetofootball). Given the fluid, relational shape, the profile leans toward zonal responsibility over a tailing marker (general knowledge).

pla.personaBrief: Sebes kept his system but adapted to the opponent: he ran warm-up games that copied the tactics of upcoming opponents and gave a four-hour tactical talk before Wembley 1953 (TFT, tier B). The identity came first, but the plan was flexed for each opponent.

res.personaBrief: The team is remembered for its style and for its unbeaten run of 32 matches (Wikipedia), and it went for goals even when winning, rather than shutting games down. The 1954 final loss is also part of the record.

sis.personaBrief: Sebes's system and the fluid roles made ordinary players look better, and everyone defended, Puskás included (Wikipedia, guidetofootball). Individual talent still decided games, which is why the answer to the winger question is left uncertain.

jog.personaBrief: The side was built on technique: Hidegkuti, Puskás and Kocsis were creative players whose quality on the ball decided games, and the team trained on ball control (TFT). Physical strength was not the criterion.

bas.personaBrief: Gap axis: no verified evidence. From general knowledge, the squad was built mostly around the Honvéd core of players in their prime, with the club as the main source, and not around veterans or youngsters ahead of their time.

lid.personaBrief: Gap axis: no verified evidence. From general knowledge, Sebes ran a disciplined, authoritarian camp in which the coach set the rules and applied them to everyone, including stars, which fits the wider verified picture of a coach who controlled every detail (TFT).
